The 72-hour food diaries are analyzed using an online dietary analysis program NutriData (Owner: Estonian National Institute for Health Development).

dmp.description: This Data Management Plan (DMP) outlines the strategy for managing, storing and sharing data generated in the project - Human Milk Iodine Concentration as a Biomarker of Iodine Status in Lactating Women and Exclusively Breastfed Infants. The plan details the types of data to be collected (including personal and sensitive data), their storage, and access information. DMP also specifies the formats for data storage and protocols for ensuring data quality, integrity and security.
dmp.ethical_issues_description:
Prior to the study, approval from the Riga Stradiņš University Ethics Committee will be received. The study will be conducted according to the guidelines laid down in the:
  • Declaration of Helsinki – Ethical Principles for Medical Research Involving Human Subjects (World Medical Association);
  • Convention for the protection of Human Rights and Dignity of the Human Being with regard to the Application of Biology and Medicine: Convention on Human Rights and Biomedicine (Council of Europe);
  • Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data, and repealing Directive 95/46/EC (General Data Protection Regulation).
Written informed consent will be obtained from all participating women before the study.
